title: Spudlight Upgrade — Storage as a Dynamical Filter and Identifiability Problem
status: archive-generated mathematical contribution extending the Spudlight/Starchforce systems formulation; standard linear-systems mathematics, not evidence for a new physical force
abstract: The storage/release part of Spudlight becomes substantially stronger when treated as a dynamical filter rather than only a stock-balance equation. A first-order store integrates input, attenuates fast variation and introduces a phase lag before release. This yields an exact impulse response, transfer function and frequency response that can be estimated from time-series data. The same formulation exposes an important identifiability result: depending on which quantities are measured, storage loss Gamma, release rate eta and upstream channel gain may or may not be separately recoverable. The project can therefore distinguish a true storage timescale from mere signal attenuation, and can state exactly what extra measurement or intervention is needed when parameters are confounded.

minimal_storage_model.state_equation: dK/dt = J_in(t) - a K(t), with a=eta+Gamma > 0
minimal_storage_model.interpretation: K is a domain-specific stock; eta is controlled/useful release and Gamma is other loss/decay. Units must remain domain-specific.

transfer_function_upgrade.meaning: The store is a one-pole low-pass filter. Slow input variation passes into release with gain eta/(eta+Gamma), while fast variation is attenuated.

frequency_response.project_interpretation: Storage naturally produces delay/smoothing. A delayed or softened manifestation of a source therefore does not require a new force; it can arise from ordinary reservoir dynamics.

periodic_input_result.scientific_use: A measured amplitude attenuation plus phase lag across forcing frequencies can estimate the storage pole and discriminate storage from a purely static gain.

case_A_stock_observed.measurements: Known calibrated J_in(t), observed K(t), but J_out not separately measured
case_A_stock_observed.identifiable: a=eta+Gamma can be identified from transient response under sufficiently informative input
case_A_stock_observed.not_identifiable: eta and Gamma are not separately identifiable from K dynamics alone because only their sum appears in dK/dt.
case_A_stock_observed.required_extra_measurement: Observe J_out=eta K or independently measure one loss channel.

case_B_release_observed.identifiable: The pole gives a=eta+Gamma and the transfer-function numerator/DC gain can identify eta; then Gamma=a-eta, subject to model adequacy and sufficient excitation.
case_B_release_observed.warning: If only normalized output shape is retained, amplitude information is lost and eta may again be confounded.

case_C_unknown_upstream_gain.model: Observed y(t)=g J_out(t)+noise with unknown static gain g
case_C_unknown_upstream_gain.confounding: The numerator becomes g eta. Without calibration, g and eta cannot generally be separated from output alone.
case_C_unknown_upstream_gain.solution: Calibrate g, add an independent stock measurement, or perform an intervention that changes eta while leaving g fixed.

identifiability_results.general_rule: Do not infer source strength, storage capacity, release efficiency and channel attenuation simultaneously from one uncalibrated output trace.

dimensionless_form.scales: Let tau=1/a, K0=J0/a and define t_tilde=t/tau, k=K/K0, j=J_in/J0.
dimensionless_form.benefit: The dimensionless pair (forcing shape, rho) separates universal first-order reservoir behavior from domain-specific units.

multi_store_extension.model: dK/dt = A K + B J_in; J_out=C K for vector stock K
multi_store_extension.meaning: Multiple reservoirs produce multiple poles/timescales rather than one universal Spudlight decay constant.
multi_store_extension.advancement_gate: Add a second reservoir only if residuals from the one-pole model show reproducible multi-timescale structure and model selection supports the extra state.
multi_store_extension.anti_pattern: Do not interpret every observed lag as a separate symbolic layer before testing a low-order linear/nonlinear reservoir model.

nonlinear_upgrade.prediction: At low K, release is approximately linear with slope J_max/K_50; at high K it saturates toward J_max.
nonlinear_upgrade.test: Compare held-out trajectories against the linear release model and penalize the extra parameter. Saturation is retained only if it improves prediction outside the calibration regime.

source_storage_channel_separation.chain: J_source -> H_source/channel -> J_in -> storage G_store -> J_out -> H_observer -> y
source_storage_channel_separation.identifiability_warning: Only the product transfer function is visible from source/output data unless intermediate states, calibrated components or interventions separate the factors.
source_storage_channel_separation.project_value: This is a precise version of source/mediator/observer ambiguity: the same observed attenuation can be caused by the source channel, storage, release or observer.

what_this_contributes: An exact dynamical response rather than only a stock-flow slogan.
A measurable phase-lag prediction for periodic forcing.
A clear statement of which Spudlight/Starchforce parameters are and are not identifiable from particular measurements.
A principled reason to add additional storage states only when data require additional timescales.
failure_conditions: Measured response has no stable low-pass/reservoir structure under repeated forcing.
Estimated eta or Gamma depends strongly on arbitrary upstream/downstream gain assumptions.
A nonlinear or multi-store model fails to improve held-out prediction over the one-pole baseline.
Physical energy, information gain and symbolic meaning are combined into one conservation equation.
